title: Communities in Schools of Laredo Marks 35 Years; 99.6% of Students Stayed in School
excerpt: Communities in Schools of Laredo marked 35 years of work in Laredo at an anniversary event Nov. 3, reporting that 99.6% of the students it served stayed in school in the 2025-26 school year and that 175 scholarships were awarded this year across 11 campuses, according to the Laredo Morning Times.
content:
Communities in Schools of Laredo marked 35 years of work in Laredo at an anniversary event on Tuesday, Nov. 3, at the International Bank of Commerce Annex, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

In the 2025-26 school year, 99.6% of the students the organization served stayed in school, 99% were promoted to the next grade, and 98% of eligible seniors graduated or earned a GED, according to the report.

The organization also awarded 175 scholarships this year across 11 campuses through the Diploma Plus Foundation, whose co-founder is Dr. Cecilia Garza, according to the report.

Executive Director Cordelia Rodriguez Sarabia said the anniversary was a chance to recognize the people who built the organization and to look ahead, highlighting a new strategic plan running through 2029, according to the report.

The event honored longtime members including Tina Treviño and Dr. Cecilia Garza, along with school and community partners, according to the report. The organization's work includes campus-based coordinators, basic-needs help, mental-health support, academic mentoring, college and career readiness, and after-school reading and math help.

Sources: Laredo Morning Times, Nov. 17, 2026.
